title: Source tax tariff basics and computed result
purpose: For employees subject to source tax, ask the denomination and whether the spouse or partner is employed. Combine these with the child and cross-border results into the full Zurich tariff code (or the Liechtenstein result), so HR no longer uses the calculator.

stories.title: State the denomination for the church-tax part of the tariff
stories.i_want: every employee who is subject to source tax to state whether they belong to the Roman Catholic, Christian Catholic or Evangelical Reformed church, or to none or another denomination
stories.so_that: the church-tax suffix (Y or N) at the end of the Zurich tariff code is correct, and employees who are not subject to source tax are not asked about their religion
stories.priority_reason: Without the denomination the tariff code cannot be completed, so HR would have to fall back to the manual calculator step that Lonio replaces (F-hr_transcript-563a9f, D-001). Asking it only of subject employees is data minimisation (G-01, F-hr_transcript-b84498).

acceptance_criteria.title: Denomination is asked only of employees subject to source tax
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee whose earlier answers (home address country, nationality, C permit, civil status and spouse details) decide whether they are subject to source tax
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee reaches the source tax questions
acceptance_criteria.then: employees subject to source tax are asked their denomination and must answer it. Employees who are not subject to source tax are not asked. The question does not depend on the type of income, because a new employee always has earned income (D-006).

acceptance_criteria.title: Denomination offers exactly the calculator's two choices
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee who is asked their denomination
acceptance_criteria.then: they choose exactly one of "Roman Catholic, Christian Catholic or Evangelical Reformed" or "None or other". The answer cannot be left empty. It is recorded for the source tax tariff code only.

acceptance_criteria.title: Denomination sets the church-tax suffix of the tariff code
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee subject to source tax who has answered the denomination question
acceptance_criteria.when: Lonio derives the church-tax suffix of the tariff code
acceptance_criteria.then: the suffix is Y for "Roman Catholic, Christian Catholic or Evangelical Reformed" and N for "None or other".

stories.title: State whether the spouse or registered partner works, for married employees and registered partners
stories.i_want: employees who are subject to source tax and married or in a registered partnership to state whether their spouse or partner is gainfully employed or receives replacement income
stories.so_that: the base tariff letter is C (spouse or partner works) or B (does not work), and nobody else is asked about a spouse's work
stories.priority_reason: The tariff letter for every married subject employee depends on it. HR names it as the extra calculator question for married employees (F-hr_transcript-09b3fe). Without it the computed tariff code (D-001) cannot be produced.

acceptance_criteria.title: Asked only of subject employees who are married or in a registered partnership
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee who has answered their civil status and whose earlier answers decide whether they are subject to source tax
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee reaches the source tax questions
acceptance_criteria.then: the question is asked, and must be answered, only if the employee is subject to source tax and is married or in a registered partnership (registered partnership counts as married for source tax). Single, divorced, widowed and separated employees count as not married for source tax and are not asked (D-003). Employees not subject to source tax are not asked.

acceptance_criteria.title: Answer is yes or no and covers replacement income
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee who is asked whether the spouse or registered partner works
acceptance_criteria.then: the question asks whether the spouse or partner is gainfully employed or receives replacement income. The answer is "yes" or "no" and cannot be left empty. It is recorded for the source tax tariff code only.

acceptance_criteria.title: Spouse's work decides the base letter C or B
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee subject to source tax who is married or in a registered partnership and has answered whether the spouse or partner works
acceptance_criteria.when: Lonio derives the base tariff letter for married employees
acceptance_criteria.then: the base letter is C if the spouse or partner works or receives replacement income, and B if not.

stories.title: Determine the tariff letter, including the cross-border letters
stories.i_want: Lonio to determine the tariff letter of every employee subject to source tax from their answers, following the Zurich calculator. That is C, B, H or A, or the cross-border letter (N, M, P or L) where the cross-border tariff applies.
stories.so_that: the letter of the computed tariff code matches what the calculator would give, without HR clicking through it
stories.priority_reason: The letter is the core of the tariff code that replaces HR's manual calculator step (F-hr_transcript-563a9f, D-001). A wrong letter gives a wrong source tax deduction.

acceptance_criteria.title: Base letter without the cross-border tariff
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee subject to source tax for whom the cross-border tariff does not apply. This covers residents of Switzerland, of countries other than Germany and Liechtenstein, and of Germany where the cross-border conditions are not met.
acceptance_criteria.then: married employees and registered partners get C if the spouse or partner works and B if not. Non-married employees (single, divorced, widowed, separated) get H if at least one child counts with H, otherwise A. There is no tariff G or Q, because replacement income does not occur for a new employee (D-006).

acceptance_criteria.title: Cross-border letters for employees living in Germany
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee subject to source tax who lives in Germany and has answered the cross-border questions
acceptance_criteria.then: if the cross-border tariff applies, the base letter is replaced: A becomes L, B becomes M, C becomes N, H becomes P. The cross-border tariff applies after a daily return with a certificate of residence, or without a daily return when a daily return is reasonable and the employee does not expect more than 60 non-return days. Otherwise the base letter stays. A certificate answered "not yet" counts as no (D-035).

stories.title: Compute and record the source tax result for HR
stories.i_want: Lonio to compute the full Zurich source tax result for every employee subject to source tax and record it for me. That is the tariff code (letter, child digit, church-tax suffix), or for Liechtenstein residents who qualify, the statement that there is in principle no source tax liability, flagged for me.
stories.so_that: I no longer sit with the employee's answers and click through the calculator, and I always have the result that fits the latest answers
stories.priority_reason: This replaces HR's manual calculator step for every employee subject to source tax (F-hr_transcript-563a9f, F-hr_transcript-4e180e), which is the product choice of D-001.

acceptance_criteria.title: No tariff code for employees not subject to source tax
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee who is not subject to source tax
acceptance_criteria.then: Lonio records that the employee is not subject to source tax. No tariff code is computed and no source tax question has been asked.

acceptance_criteria.title: Full tariff code for employees subject to source tax
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee subject to source tax who does not qualify for the Liechtenstein result
acceptance_criteria.then: Lonio records the full tariff code: the tariff letter (including the cross-border letters), then the child digit (the number of children who count, 0 without children), then the church-tax suffix Y or N. Examples are C1Y, L0Y and H2N. HR does not need the calculator for this employee.

acceptance_criteria.title: Liechtenstein residents: in principle no source tax liability, or the normal tariff code
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee living in Liechtenstein, who is therefore subject to source tax and answers the source tax and cross-border questions (D-007)
acceptance_criteria.then: if the employee returns daily, or expects at most 45 work-related non-return days, Lonio records 'In principle no source tax liability, subject to the double taxation agreement' instead of a tariff code, and flags it for HR. How HR handles the flag belongs to the later HR-side spec (D-034). If the employee expects more than 45 non-return days, Lonio records the normal tariff code.

acceptance_criteria.title: The result always follows the latest answers
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee whose answers that bear on source tax are changed later. Before submission the employee changes them. After submission HR changes them, for example after a move, a marriage, a new child or a certificate of residence handed in later.
acceptance_criteria.when: the source tax result is looked at
acceptance_criteria.then: the result (not subject, the Liechtenstein statement, or the tariff code) is derived again from the latest answers. A result that no longer matches the answers is never kept. HR's changes after submission belong to the later HR-side spec.

acceptance_criteria.title: Unexplored calculator paths are verified before go-live
acceptance_criteria.given: Lonio's computed tariff code for paths that were not explored in the calculator: the residence block for A/B/H, more than 3 children, H3N/P3N, and child results marked inferred
acceptance_criteria.when: the feature is prepared for release
acceptance_criteria.then: a domain expert compares Lonio's computed codes with the Zurich calculator for these paths, and the release waits until they match (go-live condition, see OQ-calculator-coverage). Special tariffs such as D (second job) are not computed, because they are out of scope for onboarding.
